messages.content:
You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE conductor (
    Conductor_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Age INT,
    Nationality TEXT,
    Year_of_Work INT,
    UNIQUE (Conductor_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE orchestra (
    Orchestra_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Orchestra TEXT,
    Conductor_ID INT,
    Record_Company TEXT,
    Year_of_Founded REAL,
    Major_Record_Format TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Orchestra_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Conductor_ID) REFERENCES conductor(Conductor_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE performance (
    Performance_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Orchestra_ID INT,
    Type TEXT,
    Date TEXT,
    Official_ratings_(millions) REAL,
    Weekly_rank TEXT,
    Share TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Performance_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Orchestra_ID) REFERENCES orchestra(Orchestra_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE show (
    Show_ID INT,
    Performance_ID INT,
    If_first_show bool,
    Result TEXT,
    Attendance REAL,
    FOREIGN KEY (Performance_ID) REFERENCES performance(Performance_ID)
);

Do you mean you want an SQL query that returns the **conductor table like a spreadsheet** (all rows/columns), or are you trying to **import/export** a spreadsheet?

If you just want the conductors data:

```sql
SELECT
  Conductor_ID,
  Name,
  Age,
  Nationality,
  Year_of_Work
FROM conductor
ORDER BY Conductor_ID;
```

If you tell me what columns/filters you want (e.g., only certain nationalities, sorted by years worked, include their orchestra names), I can tailor it.
you should also look for the orchestras the conductors have worked with

```sql
SELECT
  c.Conductor_ID,
  c.Name,
  c.Age,
  c.Nationality,
  c.Year_of_Work,
  o.Orchestra_ID,
  o.Orchestra AS Orchestra_Name,
  o.Record_Company,
  o.Year_of_Founded,
  o.Major_Record_Format
FROM conductor c
LEFT JOIN orchestra o
  ON o.Conductor_ID = c.Conductor_ID
ORDER BY
  c.Conductor_ID,
  o.Orchestra;
```

If you want it “spreadsheet style” with **one row per conductor** and all their orchestras combined into one cell, tell me what SQL dialect you’re using (SQLite/MySQL/Postgres), since the aggregation function differs.
make sure to get the orchestras they have actually conducted.

To ensure we only list orchestras a conductor has **actually conducted**, join through `performance` (an orchestra with no performances wouldn’t count as actually conducted):

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
  c.Conductor_ID,
  c.Name,
  c.Age,
  c.Nationality,
  c.Year_of_Work,
  o.Orchestra_ID,
  o.Orchestra AS Orchestra_Name,
  o.Record_Company,
  o.Year_of_Founded,
  o.Major_Record_Format
FROM conductor c
JOIN orchestra o
  ON o.Conductor_ID = c.Conductor_ID
JOIN performance p
  ON p.Orchestra_ID = o.Orchestra_ID
ORDER BY
  c.Conductor_ID,
  o.Orchestra;
```

If “actually conducted” should instead mean there was at least one `show` recorded (not just a performance), say so and I’ll adjust the join to include `show`.
also include the names of the conductors and orchestras too

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
  c.Name AS Conductor_Name,
  o.Orchestra AS Orchestra_Name
FROM conductor c
JOIN orchestra o
  ON o.Conductor_ID = c.Conductor_ID
JOIN performance p
  ON p.Orchestra_ID = o.Orchestra_ID
ORDER BY
  c.Name,
  o.Orchestra;
```
